decision: Revise before acceptance: long replacement gains established, but short two-match RegExp control slows in confirmation.
limitations: Completed diagnostic, not an accepted performance batch or native/Test262 checkpoint.
Case-wise ABBA confirms large-output gains. ABBAABBA short-control medians show a 13.7% slowdown for the historical regexp-one-match.js workload.

That historical global-RegExp workload actually has two matches in before-a-after. Its original source/results remain unchanged here; the next corpus keeps it as regexp-two-matches.js and adds a true one-match case.
Whole compiler comparison, not isolated per-change attribution or statistical significance.
Six corrected compiled semantic families pass; earlier harness host/oracle failures are retained.
Product build took 389 seconds versus the previous 524, but source and native-image cache state differ. No isolated same-source build-speed claim.
Private four-slot LLVM compilation reused both unchanged Intl variants; runtime-image production took 153.57 seconds with two module-cache misses and substantial function-stencil reuse.
Actual static release CLI/runner and actual Cargo producers are bound by hashes; no test shared-library link in product scores.
Process RSS, invocation samples and GC capacity are not live JavaScript heap bytes.
